messages: emma: Heads-up I'm exploring how the Threshold Preview orders notification channels. Two UX goals: (1) make the most-likely-to-fire channels visible first, (2) keep a consistent, accessible reading order for screen readers. Current Figma frames: https://figma.redwood/threshold-ordering (sketch). raj: quick thought Sorting by probability makes sense but might be surprising if users manually reorder channels elsewhere. Could we default to 'Effective priority' (calculated from route + suppression) but show a small 'sorted by: priority' chip that is interactive? claire: a11y: if we change the visual order, we must ensure DOM order matches visual order or provide aria-flowto. Screen readers rely on DOM order. Also need a programmatic announce when order changes so SR users know the context changed: e.g., "Channel order updated: Slack, Email, PagerDuty" in an aria-live region. emma: good point. I prefer DOM==visual to avoid extra ARIA complexity. For manual reorders we can keep a move-handle that updates both DOM and visual in one go. harper: copy nit instead of "Effective priority" maybe "Active priority" or "Delivery priority"? Also tiny hint under the chip: "Calculated from channel rules & suppression". Keep the hint short. raj: product edge case: when suppression silences a channel entirely, do we keep it in the list but grey it out, or hide it? My vote: keep it visible but collapsed (small row with reason) so users know why it won't notify. Hidden channels lead to confusion. claire: accessibility addendum collapsed/suppressed rows must expose the reason via aria-describedby and not only color. Use an inline "muted" icon + sr-only text. Example: Suppressed by silence window until 3pm Also ensure keyboard users can expand suppressed rows. emma: visual treatment idea suppressed rows show a faint horizontal divider + an italicized reason line; include an explicit "Why suppressed?" button that opens a tooltip with details. The row remains in DOM order. tom: implementation note if we keep DOM==visual and support drag reorder, we should use accessible dnd patterns (aria-grabbed / keyboard move with space+arrows). I can prototype keyboard-reorder UX that announces moves in a11y-live. harper: copy suggestions for the small hint: "Priority determined from route order and suppression rules." For the tooltip title: "Why this channel won't notify" (short). emma: tests: add screen reader walkthrough, keyboard-reorder unit test, and a visual regression for collapsed/suppressed state. Also add an e2e scenario: a user toggles suppression and the preview order updates and announces correctly. preview-bot: preview generated: threshold-ordering-v2 (branch: feat/threshold-ordering-ui) https://git.redwood/threshold-ordering-v2 emma: thanks all. I'll land updated frames with DOM-first order, the priority chip copy options, and the suppressed-row pattern. Posting a checklist next: copy, live-region text, keyboard-dnd behavior.
